extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition and enforcement of reciprocal discipline (public reprimand and probation) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice/service rules, respondent's opportunity to contest, probation enforcement, publication, and notice to state agencies/courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's 40-day response to contest reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks to contest imposition of his public reprimand and two years of probation pursuant to 37 C.F.R § 11.24(d), Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of Minnesota would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be filed within 40 days of the Notice and Order. The response must contain all information the respondent believes sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a timely response permits the OED Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and to impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order (mailing to last address / alternate address)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed on June 2, 2011, by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to a street address in Minneapolis, Minnesota, which was the most recent address provided by Respondent to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11. The June 2, 2011, mailing was returned as undeliverable. On July 25, 2011, a copy of the Notice and Order was mailed to an alternate street address in Minneapolis, Minnesota at which the OED Director reasonably believes Respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service is effected by mailing to the last address of record as required by 37 C.F.R. §11.11 (first-class certified mail, return receipt requested). If returned undeliverable, OED may mail to an alternate address reasonably believed to be where the respondent receives mail; successful delivery to that alternate address constitutes effective service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline when no genuine issue is shown
rubrics_metrics.description: Accordingly, it is hereby determined that: 1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and 2) the imposition of a public reprimand and two years of probation upon Respondent is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not raise a genuine issue of material fact in the 40-day response (or fails to respond), the OED Director may find no genuine issue and impose the discipline identical to that imposed by the disciplining jurisdiction (here, public reprimand and two years' probation). This is the reciprocal-discipline mechanism under 37 C.F.R. §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation to mirror state-court terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a two-year probationary period subject to the same terms and conditions imposed by the Supreme Court of Minnesota in In Re Petition of Disciplinary Action against Marc G. Kurzman, ... and commencing on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imposing reciprocal probation, the USPTO implements the same terms and conditions imposed by the originating state disciplinary order; the probation commences on the date the Final Order is signed by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and 15-day response period for alleged probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of this Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, the OED Director shall: (A) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order that Respondent be immediately suspended for up to twenty-four (24) months for the violations set forth in paragraph 6 of the Complaint; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record Respondent furnished to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation enforcement begins with the OED issuing an Order to Show Cause if it believes there's noncompliance. The Order must be sent to the last address of record and the respondent gets 15 days to respond before further action is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation to USPTO Director for immediate suspension (after consideration of response)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event after the 15-day period for response and consideration of the response, if any, received from Respondent, the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply ... the OED Director shall: (A) deliver to the USPTO Director or his designate: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response to the Order to Show Cause, if any, and (iii) evidence and argument causing the OED Director to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply ... and (B) request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend Respondent for up to twenty-four (24) months for the violations set forth in paragraph 6 of the Complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OED remains of the view that the respondent violated probation after considering any 15‑day response, OED forwards the administrative record and requests the USPTO Director to order immediate suspension up to 24 months; this is the escalation pathway to the Director for suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; The OED Director shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: NOTICE OF REPRIMAND AND PROBATION ... [text describing respondent, registration number, and bases for discipline].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO publicly posts and publishes disciplinary decisions. The Official Gazette notice must state the reprimand/probation, identify the respondent and registration number, and describe the misconduct/grounds for discipline. Disciplinary decisions are also posted in the OED Reading Room (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO must notify relevant state disciplinary authorities and courts of record admissions of the public discipline and reasons, consistent with 37 C.F.R. §11.59; this ensures interjurisdictional awareness of imposed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying grounds for discipline — trust account and commingling violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) and (b) by having been publicly reprimanded and placed on probation by the Supreme Court of Minnesota for transferring funds from a trust account to accounts in financial institutions not approved as depositories for Minnesota clients funds, failing to prepare required trust account trial balances and reconciliations resulting in client balance errors, and commingling personal and client funds by allowing a balance of earned fees to remain in the trust account for a period of at least six months, in violation of Minn. R. Prof. Conduct 1.15(a), (b), (c)(3), (d), and (f), and Appendix I thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factual misconduct supporting reciprocal discipline involves improper handling of client trust accounts: unauthorized transfers to unapproved depositories, failure to prepare trial balances/reconciliations (causing client balance errors), and commingling by retaining earned fees in the trust account for extended periods. These types of trust-account failures are grounds for public reprimand and probation under the cited Minnesota rules and form the basis for USPTO reciprocal discipline under its rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline by the USPTO is grounded in federal statute (35 U.S.C. §§2,32) and the USPTO regulations implementing disciplinary procedures (37 C.F.R. §§11.24, 11.59). Any action under §11.24 follows the procedures and grounds set forth in those provisions.
